content:
This is about functional programming with Lean, not so much formal mathematics.

In my current explorations with Lean I'm still wrapping my head around the various ways to prove invariants in my code: for example, creating a subtype, or a structure with propositions, and requiring that structure to be proved at time of construction; or alternatively creating theorems that will refuse to compile if my code allows a counterexample.

The Lean InfoView is helpful when implementing a theorem but the thing I would love to see is a way to generate any of those alternatives in the first place. This feels like fundamentally an IDE/language-server driven feature.

Imagine some structure

structure Test where
| things : SomeComplexObject
| count : Nat

Imagine we wanted to put the constraint that count was even on this. Are there IDEs that (today!) will let me highlight count, input the property I want to assert holds, and then refactor the code to (for example) insert holes in all the appropriate places I need to update? This is my dream feature.

(To be clear: I'm not proposing the IDE write the proofs or fill in the constructions - even refactoring to put typed holes in place would be a massive upgrade in ergonomics.)
